intro: Past Simple, Past Continuous, Past Perfect, Past Perfect Continuous, used to.

items.why: a finished action at a stated past time (in 2018): Past Simple.

items.q: When I got to the station, the train ___.
items.why: the train left before I arrived: Past Perfect.

items.q: I ___ TV when the lights went out.
items.why: an action in progress, interrupted by another: Past Continuous.

items.q: We were exhausted because we ___ for six hours.
items.why: duration up to a past moment (six hours): Past Perfect Continuous.

items.q: My grandfather ___ smoke, but he quit twenty years ago.
items.why: a past habit that no longer holds.

parts.title: Put the verb in brackets into the correct past form.

items.pre: By the time we arrived, the film
items.why: the film began before we arrived: Past Perfect.

items.post: dinner when her husband came home.
items.why: an action in progress when her husband came home: Past Continuous.
duration up to a past moment (all morning): Past Perfect Continuous.

items.pre: When I was a child, I
items.post: afraid of dogs, but now I love them.
items.why: a past state that is no longer true.

items.post: my old teacher in the street.
items.why: a finished action at a stated time (yesterday): Past Simple.

items.pre: The floor was wet because it
items.why: a long process with a visible result in the past (all night): Past Perfect Continuous.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: I was having breakfast when the phone was ringing.
items.corrected: I was having breakfast when the phone rang.
items.why: a short action that interrupts a process takes Past Simple, not Continuous.

items.sentence: She didn't used to like coffee.
items.corrected: She didn't use to like coffee.
items.why: after didn't the verb is "use", without -d.

items.sentence: When he came, we already ate.
items.corrected: When he came, we had already eaten.
items.why: breakfast was finished before he came: Past Perfect.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: something you used to do as a child but don't do now
items.criteria: Accept any sentence with "used to" + verb about a past habit or state that no longer holds.
items.example: I used to collect stickers when I was a child.

items.prompt: what you had been doing for some time before today's lesson started
items.criteria: Accept any sentence with "had been" + -ing that states a duration or period before the lesson began.
items.example: I had been preparing materials for two hours before the lesson started.
